emergency.label: Wasps by the door or mice in the kitchen?

maintenance_plan.name: Year-round pest plan
maintenance_plan.pitch: Quarterly exterior treatments with an inspection every visit, and free return trips if pests show up between visits. Covers ants, spiders, roaches, crickets and other common invaders.

headlines: Pests out, and a plan to keep them out.
We find how they're getting in, not just where they are.
Pest control in {{city}} that's careful around kids and pets.
Termite inspections and treatment from licensed technicians.
subheads: Licensed technicians who inspect first, treat what they find and seal the gaps pests use to get in.

services.name: General pest control
services.short: Ants, spiders, roaches, silverfish and crickets, treated inside and out.
services.long: We inspect the house for entry points and nesting areas, treat the foundation, eaves and entry points outside, and treat inside only where we find activity. Most customers go on a quarterly plan so the barrier stays in place all year.
bullets: Exterior perimeter treatment
Interior spot treatments where needed
Web and nest removal from eaves
Free return visits between scheduled treatments

services.name: Rodent control
services.short: Mice and rats trapped, removed and sealed out of the house.
services.long: Traps take care of the mice and rats inside, but more will follow unless the gaps are closed. A mouse can squeeze through an opening about a quarter inch wide, so we check around pipes, vents, garage doors and the foundation, seal openings with metal mesh and sealant, and come back to check the traps.
bullets: Inspection for entry points and droppings
Snap traps and tamper-resistant bait stations
Exclusion work with metal mesh and sealant
Follow-up visits to check and clear traps

services.name: Wasps, hornets and bees
services.short: Wasp, hornet and yellow jacket nests removed from eaves, decks and the ground.
services.long: Yellow jackets and hornets defend their nests hard, especially in late summer. We treat and remove nests safely, including ones inside walls and in the ground. Honey bee swarms go to a local beekeeper whenever they can be relocated.
bullets: Paper wasp and hornet nest removal
Ground and wall yellow jacket nests
Honey bee referrals to local beekeepers
Same-day visits when a nest is near a door

services.name: Termite treatment
services.short: Termite inspections, liquid treatments and bait systems with renewable warranties.
services.long: Subterranean termites can do damage for years before anyone sees it. We inspect the foundation, crawlspace and wood near the soil for mud tubes and damage, then recommend a liquid treatment, a bait system or both, backed by a warranty you can renew each year.
bullets: Full-home termite inspection
Liquid soil treatment around the foundation
Bait station installation and monitoring
Annual renewable warranty

services.name: Mosquito and tick control
services.short: Yard treatments every few weeks from spring through fall.
services.long: We treat the shady, damp places where mosquitoes rest (shrubs, under decks, along fences) and dump or treat standing water where they breed. Most programs run every 3 to 4 weeks during mosquito season.
bullets: Barrier treatments on foliage and resting areas
Standing water checks and larvicide
Tick treatment along wood lines and tall grass
One-time treatments before outdoor events

services.name: Bed bug treatment
services.short: Heat or product treatment, with a follow-up inspection to confirm they're gone.
services.long: Bed bugs hide in mattress seams, furniture joints and wall gaps, so treatment has to be thorough. We confirm it's bed bugs, treat with heat, products or both, and come back to check. You get a prep checklist before the visit, because how the room is prepared matters.
bullets: Inspection and identification
Whole-room heat treatment or targeted products
Prep checklist before treatment
Follow-up inspection included

services.name: Termite inspections for home sales
services.short: Wood-destroying insect reports for buyers, sellers and lenders.
services.long: Many lenders and buyers need a wood-destroying insect (WDI) report before closing. We inspect the home, fill out the standard form used in your state and send it to you, your agent and the lender, usually within a day of the inspection.
bullets: NPMA-33 or your state's required WDI form
Report sent to agents and lenders
Scheduling built around closing deadlines
Treatment quote if we find activity

process.title: Inspect
process.detail: A licensed technician checks inside and out to find what you have and how it's getting in.

process.title: Treat
process.detail: We treat the problem areas and tell you what we used and how long to keep kids and pets away.

process.title: Seal and prevent
process.detail: We seal or point out entry points and the conditions that draw pests in.

process.title: Follow up
process.detail: We come back on schedule, and in between if the pests do.

guarantees: Free return visits between scheduled treatments
Termite warranties renewable year to year
If pests come back within 30 days of a one-time treatment, we retreat at no charge
We tell you every product we apply
trust.badges_hint: A state pest control license and certified applicator credentials are required, so show the license number. QualityPro and GreenPro from NPMA are the main voluntary credentials homeowners can look up. NPMA and state association membership and BBB accreditation also help. The certifications listed are examples (NPMA is the National Pest Management Association, ESA the Entomological Society of America); keep only the ones the business holds.

faqs.q: Are the treatments safe for my kids and pets?
faqs.a: We use EPA-registered products and apply them according to the label, which is the law. For most exterior treatments, keep kids and pets off treated areas until they dry, usually an hour or two. Before we leave, we tell you what we used and any steps to take.

faqs.q: How much does pest control cost?
faqs.a: The first visit usually costs more than follow-ups because it includes a full inspection and a heavier treatment. Ongoing quarterly service for an average home commonly runs $100 to $300 per visit. Termites, bed bugs and rodent exclusion are priced by the job after we inspect.

faqs.q: Why quarterly service instead of one treatment?
faqs.a: Exterior treatments break down over a few months from sun and rain, and new pests keep arriving from outside. Quarterly visits keep the barrier in place. For a one-time problem, like a single wasp nest, a one-time visit is fine.

faqs.q: Do I need to leave the house during treatment?
faqs.a: For most general pest treatments, no. For bed bug heat treatments and some flea or roach treatments, you'll need to be out for a few hours, and we'll tell you ahead of time.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have termites?
faqs.a: Look for mud tubes on the foundation, piles of discarded wings near windows in spring, wood that sounds hollow or paint that bubbles. Many homes show no signs until the damage turns up during a repair. An annual inspection is the most reliable way to catch them.

faqs.q: How long until I stop seeing bugs?
faqs.a: You may see more pests for a week or two after a treatment as they're flushed out, then activity should drop off. If you're still seeing them after two weeks, call us and we'll come back.

faqs.q: Can you get rid of mice for good?
faqs.a: Trapping alone won't, because new mice follow the same paths in. Sealing the entry points is what keeps them out, so exclusion work is part of every rodent job we quote.

faqs.q: Do you handle raccoons, squirrels or snakes?
faqs.a: Wildlife removal often needs a separate state permit. We'll tell you whether we handle it in {{area}} or refer you to a licensed wildlife control company.
